title: Drop and Contact
premise: Orsen Galloway, a private security contractor who cleans up deniable messes for clients nobody trusts, is approached by a stranger named Ilse Varga claiming Orsen once saved her life — a favor Orsen has no memory of performing. The debt is real, though: it traces back to Halcyon Row, the black-site training program that built Orsen and erased the years that made her. As Ilse pulls her into hunting the network's surviving architects, Orsen discovers the program is being reactivated with a new class of assets, and the only way to stop it is to burn every record — including the ones proving who she was before. In the end, Orsen chooses love and memory over duty, torching the archive at the cost of her own cover, and walks away from the trade with Ilse, finally owing nothing to anyone.
about_author: Wendell Oyelaran is a former logistics analyst who spent a decade moving through the gray corridors of defense contracting before turning to fiction. He writes thrillers about people whose loyalties were manufactured for them, drawing on his fascination with institutional memory and the debts we never agreed to owe.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Between contracts in Rotterdam, Orsen is approached by Ilse Varga, who thanks her for saving her life in Lagos three years ago — an operation Orsen has no record of and no memory of. The emotional beat: unease dressed as professional courtesy, as Orsen realizes someone else knows her history better than she does.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse explains she isn't asking for gratitude — she's repaying a debt by warning Orsen that Halcyon Row, the program that trained her, is reactivating under a new shell company. Emotional beat: reluctant trust between two women bound by a past one of them can't remember.

chapters.title: Clients Nobody Trusts
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen runs a routine protection detail for a defense broker and notices surveillance patterns identical to ones from her forgotten Lagos op. Emotional beat: the creeping suspicion that her current work was designed to keep her exactly where someone wanted her.

chapters.title: Redacted Years
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Digging into her own service records, Orsen finds a fourteen-month gap papered over with commendations. She confronts her old handler, Marcus Teale, who stonewalls then warns her to drop it. Emotional beat: grief for a self she was never allowed to know.

chapters.title: The Lagos File
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse shares what she survived in Lagos: a Halcyon wet-work op gone wrong, saved by a contractor whose face she never forgot. Emotional beat: guilt and gratitude tangled together, and the first hint that Ilse knows more about Orsen than she's saying.

chapters.title: Tail Numbers
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Following the shell company's money through aviation records, Orsen identifies a decommissioned airfield in Moldova receiving irregular cargo flights. Emotional beat: cold focus hardening into purpose — this is a hunt now, not an inquiry.

chapters.title: Teale's Confession
chapters.summary: Marcus Teale's POV. Cornered, Teale admits he helped erase Orsen's gap year and reveals the program kept 'leverage files' on every graduate. Emotional beat: a broken man's shame, and the revelation that Orsen's amnesia may have been administered, not accidental.

chapters.title: What They Built Me For
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen tests her own conditioning and discovers embedded protocols still live in her — failsafes she can trigger without knowing. Emotional beat: horror at finding the enemy inside her own reflexes, and resolve to map every tripwire.

chapters.title: Moldova, Off Season
chapters.summary: Orsen and Ilse's alternating POV. Reconnaissance of the airfield reveals a training compound housing a new class of recruits, some barely legal age. Emotional beat: fury transmuted into discipline; Ilse and Orsen become true partners here.

chapters.title: The Architect
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen identifies Dr. Anselm Reiter, the program's designer, alive and running the new iteration under a dead man's name. Emotional beat: the personal made operational — this is no longer a network, it's a face.

chapters.title: Dead Drop Protocol
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse is made by a counter-surveillance team and barely escapes, burning their safehouse in the process. Emotional beat: fear and the first fracture of trust — did Ilse get sloppy, or was she bait?

chapters.title: Leverage
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Reiter activates one of Orsen's embedded failsafes remotely, forcing her to stand down mid-operation and prove the program still owns her body if not her mind. Emotional beat: violation and terror, followed by defiance — she starts designing counters.

chapters.title: The Recruit
chapters.summary: New character Danya's POV. A young recruit inside the compound begins questioning her handlers after witnessing a disciplinary disappearance. Emotional beat: innocence colliding with machinery, giving the enemy institution a human face worth saving.

chapters.title: Counters
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Working with a disgraced neuroscientist, Orsen learns to recognize and short-circuit her triggers, at the cost of blinding migraines and fraying control. Emotional beat: painful reclamation — taking back her own nervous system piece by piece.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: Orsen and Ilse's POV. On the eve of the assault, Orsen and Ilse admit what they've become to each other, knowing the mission may require one of them to die or worse. Emotional beat: tenderness sharpened by mortality; a promise made without conditions.

chapters.title: Infiltration
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen walks into the compound using her own Halcyon credentials, posing as a returning asset, while Ilse runs the perimeter. Emotional beat: walking back into the machine willingly, every step a controlled act of self-betrayal turned weapon.

chapters.title: Reiter's Offer
chapters.summary: Reiter's POV. Reiter offers Orsen restoration of her missing memories in exchange for becoming the new program's director — he claims she was always its finest product. Emotional beat: seduction of the self, the temptation to be made whole by the very hand that unmade her.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen refuses, triggers the compound's fire-suppression and data-destruction systems manually, and fights her way out as the archive burns — including the records of who she was. Emotional beat: choosing an unknown future over a curated past.

chapters.title: Extraction
chapters.summary: Ilse and Danya's POV. Ilse extracts Orsen wounded; Danya leads six recruits out through the cargo tunnel as the facility falls. Emotional beat: desperate, costly triumph — lives saved balanced against everything lost.

chapters.title: Loose Ends
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen hunts down the last off-site node in Prague and ends Reiter's network permanently, declining to kill him in favor of delivering him to journalists. Emotional beat: cold completion, and the discovery that vengeance feels smaller than expected.

chapters.title: Owing Nothing
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen settles accounts: Teale gets his exposure, the rescued recruits get new names, and Orsen formally dissolves her contracting practice. Emotional beat: lightness after a lifetime of debt — the stranger's favor finally repaid in full.

chapters.title: Drop and Contact
chapters.summary: Orsen and Ilse's POV, closing scene. Somewhere quiet on the Atlantic coast, Orsen begins writing down the memories she does have, building a self from choice rather than design, with Ilse beside her. Emotional beat: peace earned, not granted — love chosen freely where duty was imposed.
